data.narrative:
Longshot Space is a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Mike Grace and Nathan Saichek that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though narrow peer matching at the seed stage in Space & Aerospace proved limited.

Of the three triangulation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the $10M total raised as a proxy for entry valuation and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression in venture capital. This yields an implied valuation of $25M. Peer-median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the Space & Aerospace sector (0 qualifying narrow peers from 11 total sector companies). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple could not be applied because the target's revenue is not on file, a common limitation for private companies.

The triangulated range stands at $21M (low), $25M (median), and $29M (high), derived from sensitivity bounds around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrower private peer data at seed stage and lack of revenue visibility to cross-check via public multiples. The analysis is anchored to stage-progression mechanics rather than direct market comparables, which limits conviction.
